### Observed differences

- Six activities — A27 and the group A36, A37, A42, A43, A44 — appeared in only about half of the traces in the earlier window (roughly 52 in 100, about 0.5 occurrences per trace); in the later window each appears in essentially every trace (200 in 200), about once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the earlier window, A25 led almost always to A28 (about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions), and A26 split its outgoing transitions between A27 (about 48 in 100) and the five group activities (about 52 in 100 combined); in the later window A25 leads into the group (about 15–24 in 100 per activity, together essentially all) and A26 leads to A27 in about 98 in 100. [DIR001, DIR002]
- In the earlier window, each group activity still led to A31 in about 14–27 in 100 of its outgoing transitions alongside transitions to the other group members; in the later window these transitions to A31 are gone and each group activity instead leads to A28 in about 14–24 in 100. A27's transition to A31 (about 96–98 in 100) is unchanged. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- The relations changed accordingly: A27 and each group activity were near-perfect alternatives before (together in only about 1–2 in 100 traces) and now always occur together with the group activity first (about 99 in 100); A26 and A28, which previously preceded the group activities, now follow them (about 99 in 100); A27 now co-occurs with A25 and with A26 in every trace, after them, where before it shared a trace with each in only about 49 in 100. [REL001, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- Event positions moved in the same direction (event positions, not clock times): the group activities' mean relative position fell from about 0.58 to about 0.40, A28's rose from about 0.39 to 0.48, A26's from 0.53 to 0.61 and A27's from 0.59 to 0.63; A25 occurs slightly earlier (about 0.35 to 0.32) and A31 slightly later (about 0.64 to 0.66). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- The internal order of the group shows no fixed sequence in either window — both orders appear in similar shares (for example, A36 before A37 in about 25 vs 27 in 100 traces before, and about 47 vs 53 in 100 after). [REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038, REL039]
- Ordered-pair evidence agrees: A36 followed by A28, and A43 followed by A28, within five steps were observed in only 1 trace each before and now occur in about 197 in 200 traces, while A42 followed by A31 within five steps fell from about 102 traces to 2; the thin side of each rests on only 1–2 observations. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the either/or routing after A26 was removed and the five-activity group was repositioned. In the earlier window, a trace ran A25 → A28 → A26 and then either A27 → A31 (about 48 in 100 traces) or the group A36/A37/A42/A43/A44 → A31 (about 52 in 100), the two branches being near-perfect alternatives; in the later window, every trace runs A25 → the group, in an unfixed internal order → A28 → A26 → A27 → A31. A27 and the five group activities thereby changed from optional, mutually exclusive alternatives, each present in about half of the traces, into mandatory steps present in every trace, and A28 changed from following A25 directly to following the group. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL008, REL015, REL020, POS004]

The change is shown directly by the successor changes at A25, A26 and all five group activities and by the relational order flips (the group now precedes A26, A28 and A27, where it previously followed them or excluded A27), with the participation and position shifts agreeing in direction; 66 items qualified against roughly 1 expected for an unchanged process, so chance cannot account for the pattern as a whole. Limitations: the evidence shows event order within traces, not clock time, and cannot distinguish a strictly sequential group from parallel or interleaved execution of its five activities, since both orders occur in similar shares in both windows; the LAG agreement rests on only 1–2 observations in one window, and the two windows remain finite samples. [REL030, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
